description.value: Galey Farms is a family-run farm market, corn maze, and miniature railway in the Blenkinsop Valley on the southern tip of Vancouver Island. During the growing season they sell their own-grown strawberries, corn, potatoes, broccoli, kale, blueberries, pumpkins, and squash alongside local honey products, making it a genuine source of fresh food rather than a convenience stop. The farm sits directly adjacent to the Lochside Regional Trail and won Canada's top ecological award in 2002 for restoring a 600-metre section of Blenkinsop Creek alongside that trail.

The front page states the market is expected to reopen end of May 2026 weather permitting after an accident closed the building, while the Location & Hours subpage still reads 'Now Closed for the Season', making confirmed_open ambiguous. No website content addresses bike parking, water refill, or most optional amenities; the Environment page explicitly notes the farm is adjacent to the Lochside Regional Trail, which is relevant context for cycling tourists.
